title: a render ran out of VRAM inside ComfyUI (torch OOM)
evidence: 1 ComfyUI torch-OOM(s) in the last 48h; newest comfyui-comfyui-1789999255-213957-1.log (8.3h old); died at 21.32 GiB allocated, 78.00 MiB requested, device limit 23.52 GiB; the budget was 21719.11 MB usable / 21448.72 MB loaded; newest launch args: --listen 0.0.0.0 --reserve-vram 5. This is the CAUSE of the HTTP-500 / timeout rows tracked as render-execution-error: ComfyUI sizes its dynamic-VRAM budget from FREE memory, so the emptier the card the MORE it loads -- over-committing is fatal, offloading is merely slower. Judge the fix by the budget line: a launch carrying --reserve-vram (bin/comfyui_harness.sh COMFY_RESERVE_VRAM) should hold 'usable' well under the ~21719 MB that failed; if it still reads ~21 GB, the flag did not reach the budget (check comfy_aimdo's simple_vram_headroom path against the runtime .venv). Self-closes when no OOM is inside the window.

notes.note: 2026-09-22 01:4xZ ops-triage: DECIDED -- the fix stands and this item is now its VERDICT INSTRUMENT. (1) WHY THIS ENTRY EXISTS: a torch OOM inside ComfyUI was invisible to the board -- the cgroup sampler sees no oom_kill (the process survives the failed allocation) and the Rails row carries only whatever the renderer did NEXT -- so the cause could only be found by hand-reading a ComfyUI log on the NAS. The new probe check reads the ComfyUI job log and files this entry WITH THE BUDGET LINE, so a recurrence names the numbers instead of the symptom, and an OOM whose retry RECOVERS (which leaves no failed row anywhere) becomes visible. Verified against real data: it found the 00:05Z block exactly (died at 21.32 GiB allocated, 78.00 MiB requested, device limit 23.52 GiB; budget was 21719.11 MB usable / 21448.72 MB loaded) and correctly excluded the 09-17 OOM that sits outside the 48h window; tc_ops.py selftest 292 assertions / 0 failures (9 new). (2) PLUMBING VERIFIED OFFLINE, one level deeper than last pass: --reserve-vram reaches the budget through TWO paths -- EXTRA_RESERVED_VRAM (comfy/model_management.py:883-884) and comfy_aimdo simple_vram_headroom (main.py:72-81 -> control.init) -- and the RUNTIME venv is /mnt/fscache/essdee/ComfyUI/.venv, whose comfy_aimdo is 0.5.5 and whose control.init DOES accept simple_vram_headroom (read at .venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/comfy_aimdo/control.py:62-67). TRAP for the next verifier: the SIBLING venv/ directory holds comfy_aimdo 0.4.3, whose init takes no such parameter -- main.py catches the TypeError and falls back to NO headroom -- so reading the wrong venv concludes the flag is a silent no-op. The harness launches with .venv (bin/comfyui_harness.sh:90). (3) THE PREDICTION IS STILL UNVERIFIED: no render has run since the fix landed (commit 6a01bb6 at 20:43 EDT; the last render window was 20:01-20:19), so no live budget line exists yet. The harness now logs its launch args verbatim, so the next render yields both facts at once (args + usable). (4) RESIDUAL RISK, named so it is read rather than felt: 5 GiB is subtracted from whatever is free AT LAUNCH, so if a co-tenant holds ~8 GiB (free ~13 GiB) the budget lands near 8 GiB -- below the 15.3 GiB that is PROVEN to render in 95.6s. If the next render shows offload thrash or timeouts rather than an OOM, lower COMFY_RESERVE_VRAM to 2 rather than removing the flag. No further change until a render reads; the entry self-closes 48h after the last OOM.

2026-09-22 01:5xZ ops-triage: ADDENDUM from PRIMARY EVIDENCE, not from the note above (psql on comfyui_jobs, 8h window): 7564 failed 00:01Z-00:05Z carrying the OOM text; 7565 completed 00:05Z-00:09Z; 7566 failed 00:05Z (ComfyUI API error: HTTP 500); 7567 completed 00:12Z-00:17Z. So the bounded retry pair RECOVERED ON ITS OWN and NO RENDER WAS LOST -- the cost of one over-commit was two wasted jobs, which makes the reserve-vram fix a throughput/robustness fix, NOT a data-loss one (the earlier framing of a lost render is corrected here). It also sharpens why this entry exists: the OOM text DID sit in the failed row 7564, but the board interpolates only the NEWEST failed row (7566, the HTTP 500) and its prose attributed that to the workflow payload -- the cause sat one row behind the symptom, unread. This entry carries the cause WITH its budget numbers and the launch args that were in force, which no DB row does. Check comment corrected to match. tc_ops.py selftest 292 assertions / 0 failures.

2026-09-22 02:5xZ ops-triage: VERDICT IN -- the reserve-vram fix is VERIFIED on a live render and this entry's falsifiable prediction was correct. Evidence, all from the render that ran 02:35:25Z-02:42:19Z (ComfyuiJob 7568, PipelineRun 482, our scheduler job comfyui-1790038865-1557706-1, launched through bin/comfyui_harness.sh): (1) the launch line, from the harness log -- args='--listen 0.0.0.0 --reserve-vram 5', with the instrument asserting it on the LIVE pid (/proc/1736856/cmdline) inside its own unit cgroup; (2) the budget line moved exactly as predicted: 'loaded partially; 16887.89 MB usable, 16518.44 MB loaded, 6181.69 MB offloaded', then '16239.08 MB usable ... 6829.75 MB offloaded' -- against the FATAL '21719.11 MB usable, 21448.72 MB loaded' that died 78 MiB short at 21.32 GiB allocated on the 23.52 GiB device; (3) 'Prompt executed in 410.46 seconds', no torch.OutOfMemoryError, no HTTP 500, ComfyuiJob status=completed, and the cgroup sampler (log/comfyui_telemetry.jsonl) recorded oom_events=0 / oom_kill_events=0 with mem_peak 56.9 GB (MemoryMax=infinity, no cap). MEASURED TRADE, recorded so the next pass does not re-derive it: the same multi-stage workflow took 256s (job 7565) and 300s (job 7567) WITHOUT the reserve and 410s WITH it -- ~1.4x slower from the extra ~6.2 GB offloaded (vs 1.3-2.1 GB offloaded), which is offload cost, NOT thrash and NOT a timeout. The earlier note set the trigger for lowering COMFY_RESERVE_VRAM to 2 as 'offload thrash or timeouts'; neither occurred, and reserve 2 would leave usable ~20.9 GB, too close to the 21.7 GB budget line that was fatal. DECISION: keep --reserve-vram 5; no further change. This entry stays probe-managed and self-closes 48h after the last OOM (2026-09-24 ~00:05Z), re-firing with fresh numbers if one recurs.

2026-09-22 05:4xZ ops-triage: DECISION -- accept the measured throughput cost of --reserve-vram 5 and keep the value. New primary evidence (comfyui_jobs created_at/completed_at pairs): renders ran 261s (7565) and 304s (7567) BEFORE the reserve, 412s (7568) and 402s (7569) AFTER it -- the ~6.2 GB of extra offload costs ~110-140s per render. That now overruns the growth tick: its producer budget is SYNC_BUDGET_SECONDS=360 and its foreground tool call is SIGKILLed at ~420s, so a ~410s render consumes the whole window and the tick's OWN post-actions (import/caption/slot) are routinely killed. Evidence: PipelineRuns 480/482/483/484 were each marked failed by the reconciler with the honest reason 'sync producer Growth::ContentGenerator left this run non-terminal with no job in flight (the producer process was killed before it wrote a terminal status)'. CONTENT IS NOT LOST: Growth::AbandonedRenderWorker (armed in the always-on sidekiq; verified this pass -- exactly 1 job of that class in Sidekiq::ScheduledSet, next 05:39:00Z) recovered posts 349/350/351 at 03:44/04:48Z. WHY ACCEPT: (i) lowering COMFY_RESERVE_VRAM leaves ~20.9 GB usable against the 21.7 GB budget line that was fatal, re-risking the OOM the flag exists to prevent; (ii) the queue is AT TARGET (publishable=21, dry_out 2026-09-28T14:00Z) so recovery latency costs no content; (iii) a killed tick costs one render window, not a render. REVERSAL TRIGGER (a threshold, not a vibe): queue below target or dry_out inside ~3 days, or 2 consecutive ticks whose completed render is still unrecovered past 60 min -- then fix the producer LAUNCH MODE (run it detached in its own cgroup so post-actions are not inside the caller's window), not the VRAM flag. Probe-owned: self-closes 48h after the last OOM (2026-09-24 ~00:05Z).

2026-09-22 06:3xZ ops-triage: TRIGGER CORRECTED against a measured counterexample -- the reversal trigger recorded in the 05:4xZ note ('queue below target or dry_out inside ~3 days') FIRES ON THE HEALTHY STEADY STATE and would have triggered a launch-mode change on a working system. Measured this pass: publishable=19 against target=21 at 06:11Z decomposes EXACTLY into 21 status_rows - 1 age-gate hold (post 345) - 1 due-but-paced post (329, held by scheduling:post_scheduled pacing: 'Pacing: holding 1 further due post(s) ... still due, releases on the next tick'), plus post 321 published at 06:00Z by the hourly publisher. A queue below target mid-hour is the NORMAL reading of a system that paces one release per tick and tops up one render per tick -- not evidence of starvation. CORRECTED TRIGGER (interval, not point): act only if (a) dry_out under 3 days, OR (b) the shortfall FAILS TO CLOSE across 2 or more consecutive hourly ticks (what closes it is the render+salvage pair: posts 348@02:01Z, 349/350@03:44Z, 351@04:48Z this window), OR (c) 2 or more ticks whose completed render is still unrecovered past 60 min. ALSO RECORDED, because that trigger named a fix already rejected: 'run the producer detached in its own cgroup' was DECIDED AGAINST (item growth-tick-launch-mode, closed 2026-09-21 11:22 -- 'This is a BUDGET rather than a detached launch on purpose: step 4 GPU release must run after the producer returns, so backgrounding it would let the shutdown SIGTERM ComfyUI mid-render'). DECISION UNCHANGED: keep --reserve-vram 5, no change.

ACCEPTANCE HOLDS, now with a longer track record -- the --reserve-vram 5 fix has survived 5 consecutive renders with zero OOM: ComfyuiJob 7568 (415s), 7569 (402s), 7570 (723s under co-tenant pressure), 7571 (406s), 7572 (354s), all status=completed between 02:42Z and 07:07Z on 09-22; no torch.OutOfMemoryError anywhere in log/development.log since the 00:05Z pair, and the budget line stays in the proven envelope (usable ~13.5-16.9 GB vs the FATAL 21719.11 MB). The throughput cost accepted at 05:4xZ is unchanged (400-720s per render vs 256-304s before the reserve). No new decision needed; probe-owned (48h window, newest OOM 09-22 00:0xZ) so it self-closes ~09-24 00:01Z.
